summary.text: An 83-year-old white woman with seropositive NMOSD diagnosed in 2014, maintained on mycophenolate mofetil 1,000 mg daily, with Parkinson disease and hypertension (current medications carbidopa-levodopa, gabapentin, losartan), presented to the emergency department with acute unilateral painful loss of vision in the right eye described as a “lavender haze”; altered mental status was present at admission.

Examination showed visual acuity 20/40 OD and counting fingers at 3 feet OS, a relative afferent pupillary defect OS, optic disc pallor OS and Ishihara 13/14 OD and 0/14 OS, with hiccups, nausea, vomiting, hypersomnolence, headaches, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication and weight loss denied. Admission temperature was 97.6°F; laboratory studies showed hemoglobin 13.3 g/dL, leukocytes 8.0 × 10^(3)/µL, platelets 272 × 10^(3)/µL, CRP 1.50 mg/dL (elevated), ESR 22 mm/h, AQP4-IgG positive by FACS (1:100) and MOG-IgG negative. She was described as stable until readmission with blurred vision and worsened mental status.

NMOSD relapse versus infection-related pseudo-flare was considered; empirical intravenous methylprednisolone was given, after which mental status worsened and hallucinations developed. MRI of brain, orbits and spine with contrast showed no new lesions or optic nerve enhancement and no acute demyelination but left optic nerve atrophy; temporal artery ultrasound was negative.

Urinalysis (leukocyte esterase positive, 24 WBC/hpf, bacteriuria) and urine culture (Klebsiella oxytoca, 10^(5) cfu/mL) confirmed a urinary tract infection. Steroids were discontinued and doxycycline and amoxicillin-clavulanate were started; mental status improved and hallucinations resolved. The episode was adjudicated as an infection-related pseudo-relapse, not an NMOSD relapse. She lacked typical signs of infection, which the authors considered unsurprising given her immunosuppressive therapy.

At neuro-ophthalmic examination 3 weeks later she had returned to baseline status, with visual acuity 20/50 OD and count fingers OS, Ishihara 13/14 OD and 0/14 OS, Humphrey 24-2 mean deviation −0.78 decibels OD with a nonspecific scatter defect, a dense central scotoma with superior altitudinal defect OS, and RNFL 103 µm OD and 57 µm OS with inferior sectoral atrophy OS.
